case_title: KALA SINGH @ GURNAM SINGH v. STATE OF PUNJAB
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304 Part II r/w s.34; IPC s.201
mitigating_circumstances: Sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel; no pre-meditation; no intention to cause death or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302/34 and s.201 IPC
high_court_outcome: Modified conviction to s.304 Part-I/34 IPC
offence_finally_established: s.304 Part-II/34 IPC and s.201 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused and the deceased had a sudden fight over a stolen pigeon. The co-accused, who had a rod, struck the deceased on the head with the rod, causing his death. The accused and the co-accused then disposed of the deceased's body in a canal. The incident occurred after consuming liquor, and there was no pre-meditation. The scuffle happened in the heat of passion due to a sudden quarrel. The deceased did not respond after the blow, and the body was moved to the canal.
